**Written Statement Regarding Amara Okafor — October 27**

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing about the concern you raised regarding Amara’s ride home on Tuesday, October 27. I understand that having your daughter returned to school instead of dropped at her stop was frightening and upsetting. I am sorry she had a difficult afternoon, and I want to explain what happened from my perspective. My intention was to follow the district’s safety procedure and make sure Amara was supervised.

I was driving Bus 41 on Route 9 for Fairmont Elementary. Amara is a kindergarten student, and the green tag on her bag indicates that an adult must be present at her stop. We arrived at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at approximately 3:52 p.m., about two minutes after the scheduled time. I waited until about 3:55, but I did not see an adult at the corner.

The district procedure for kindergarten students is that if no adult is present at the stop, the student remains on the bus and is returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. At 3:56, I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. I still had three stops to make and 14 other students on the bus, so I could not leave the bus to search across the street or leave the students unsupervised.

I understand you told the office that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and waved to me. I did not see you. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street, which may have affected what I could see, but I do not want to assume what happened from your position. I was focused on the stop and the students in my care. As we pulled away, I was telling a fourth grader in seat 2 to sit back down. I was not laughing or dismissing your concern.

I brought Amara back to Fairmont Elementary at approximately 4:31 p.m. and walked her into the office myself, where I left her with Mrs. Petrakis. Amara appeared to be doing well. She was coloring on her folder and asked if she could ride more. I told her we were taking a little extra trip. I know that does not change how worrying the situation may have been for you, and I understand why you wanted to know she was safe.

I respectfully ask that the district review and preserve the bus camera footage from the stop and the time the bus pulled away. I believe it may help clarify what was visible from the bus and what occurred as we departed. I am also asking that the review include the dispatch communication and the school’s contact with you, if those records are available.

For future stops, it would help if you could wait on the bus side of the street, where I can more readily see you, or step out of your car as the bus approaches. I understand that may not always be convenient, and I am not saying you did anything wrong. I want us to have a clear way to identify one another so Amara can be handed off safely and without confusion.

I have driven school buses for 28 years and have not had a prior write-up. I take my responsibility for the students on my bus seriously. I have encountered a similar no-adult-at-the-stop situation in the past, involving another family, and followed the same procedure. My decision on October 27 was based on the district rule and my responsibility to keep all the students supervised—not on any wish to upset you or inconvenience your family.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I hope we can resolve this in a way that helps everyone feel confident about her ride home. Thank you for reading my account.

Respectfully,

**[Driver’s Name]**  
Bus 41, Route 9  
**Date:** [Date of statement]
